content:
Hi. I've recently been working on PRs (#41082, #37631) relating to Function.prod and some related things.

#41082 introduces Function.diag, the map α → α × α which duplicates its argument (i.e. it is Function.prod id id).

#37631 is too large and I am slowly hiving it off into smaller PRs.

@Monica Omar has suggested that I have a discussion here about notation. My proposed notation for Function.diag is:
a) it is spelled as it is when consider it as a function.
b) in application we use △(a) = (a, a).

I think it would also be desirable to have a notation for docs#Function.prod. My proposed notation for Function.prod f g is f ×ᶠ g, by analougy with docs#Set.prod. There's actually an argument that, just as SProd is a typeclass, we should make FProd a typeclass - that would then also cover things like MonoidHom.prod.

I also wanted to highlight that we have things like docs#MonoidHom.prodMap, and in theory it would be perfectly reasonable to have Function.prodMap, which is precisely (f ∘ Prod.fst) ×ᶠ (g ∘ Prod.snd). But this is equal to (indeed reflexively equal to) Prod.map. This raises another question: is Function.prod even in the right namespace?

The dual to docs#Function.prod, such as it is, is docs#Sum.elim. That isn't quite true - because Sum.elim is for non-dependent functions. You could make it for dependent functions - this is just the recursor on Sum! Still, it is clear that this is the dual. In a similar way docs#Sum.map is dual to Prod.map and indeed one could define Function.sumMap in a similar way to above. And we could also have the "codiag", the map α ⊕ α → α that extracts an α from the sum type. We already sort of have some of this but only as part of the Equiv story. You could imagine called this Sum.codiag and my Function.diag Prod.diag instead, incidentally.

So there's four questions:
a) what is a good notation for Function.diag
b) what is a good notation for Function.prod
c) is it useful to have Function.prodMap, which allows Prod.map to be used with different dot notation (i.e. the operator rather than the operand is the subject of the .)
d) What is to be done about the fact that there is a fundamental inconsistency between Sum and Prod with these operations?

I would also like to do some work to consistently have docs#Function.prod supported by, say, fun_prop for various properties - we tend to use the form a la docs#Continuous.prodMk but it's far from clear to me that that is the right choice.

https://gist.github.com/wrenna-robson/780b992099671e207fb7c334d49955cf

This is what codiag would look like, by the way.

Not entirely clear to me what the proper dependent version (that is, using dependent functions, i.e. Pi types) should look like for sum.

protected def sum {α β} {γ : α ⊕ β → Sort*} (f : ∀ i, γ (.inl i)) (g : ∀ i, γ (.inr i))
    (i : α ⊕ β) : γ i := match i with | .inl a => f a | .inr b => g b

Something like this kind of works. But if we were using that form, then really we should use:

protected def prod {ι} {α : ι → Type* × Type*} (f : ∀ i, (α i).1) (g : ∀ i, (α i).2) (i : ι) :
    (α i).1 × (α i).2 := (f i, g i)

And this is clearly just quite weird.
Hmm. Not really sure how to get people engaged in this. Normally people are always up for bikeshedding some notation!

I think the notation for the diagonal is fine. How about we have one PR for the definition and one just for the notation? That way you can use it more throughout the library so people can see if they like it or not (currently the PR only uses it once, if I remember correctly)
I would be happy to drop the notation from the current PR and add it, hopefully maybe in a future PR that added Function.prod notation.
I wouldn’t introduce both notation in a single PR. It’s better to have one PR do one thing so people can focus on it properly
But yeah, please drop it from the current PR :)

Can I ask how introducting Function.diag will work with your PR #38380, which renames diag to diagMap: should #38380 update to use functionDiag instead? Should we wait for #41082 before reviewing #38380 or vice versa?

Yeah good question - obviously I hadn't really thought how they'd work together. I think the decision to rename to diagMap in #38380 is not correct probably - I think it's just the one lemma whose name changes? So I'd keep it as range_diag I think.
